A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same NKQ research and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Content can be matched reliably despite extensive reformatting and the addition of Appendix F.5.

before.justification: Section 5 reports original synthetic, financial-risk, healthcare, and Bayesian optimization experiments. Appendix Figures 5–6 report hyperparameter ablations and multilevel-method comparisons.

after.justification: The original experimental outcomes in Figures 2–6 are retained, including estimation errors, Bayesian optimization performance, ablations, and multilevel comparisons.

M1.justification: The NKQ estimator in equations (7)–(9), CKQ in equation (10), and MLKQ construction in Appendix D are retained. Appendix F.5 explains the existing change-of-variable and weight-precomputation procedure rather than introducing a new component.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same synthetic dimension sweep, butterfly-option risk problem, healthcare EVPPI model, and Dropwave, Ackley, and Cosine8 optimization tasks. Appendix F.5 documents existing tasks; predictive entropy search is mentioned only as future work.

E2.justification: The experiment-specific comparator sets remain unchanged: NMC in synthetic and ablation studies; NMC, NMC (QMC), and MLMC in finance and healthcare; NMC and MLMC in Bayesian optimization; and MLKQ in Figure 6.

E3.justification: Section 3 replaces a shared lambda0 with stage-specific lambda0,X and lambda0,Theta, retaining the same search grid. Equation (F.42) changes the synthetic integrand's norm subscripts from 2.5/2.5 to 2s/2. This is a changed written specification, but the unchanged reference value and plots leave its intended implementation unclear; neither edit establishes that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The sample-allocation and dimension analyses in Figure 2, regularization/lengthscale/kernel ablations in Figure 5, and supplementary MLKQ comparisons in Figure 6 are retained. No new robustness test or supplementary empirical analysis is reported.

E5.justification: Figure 2 still reports 1000 independent runs, and Figures 3–4 still report 100. Both versions use 25%–75% quantile shading, with no added repeated-run information, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Figures 2–6 retain the same empirical curves and findings. The financial experiment's fitted exponents remain 2.97, 2.74, 1.90, and 1.91. No empirical result entries are added or removed; the corrected theoretical cost expressions are assessed under T1.

T1.justification: Theorem 1(1) replaces bounds on density L-infinity norms with pointwise positive lower and upper bounds, matching Appendix A's requirements. Section 5 corrects NMC cost from Delta^(-1/3) to Delta^(-3), and Section 5/Appendix F.2 correct inverted NKQ dimension/smoothness ratios. The principal convergence bounds and appendix proof arguments remain.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: NKQ, faster convergence under sufficient smoothness, and empirical advantages across the existing applications. New future-work discussion does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly identifies finding a suitable transformation map as a practical challenge. It adds discussion of unresolved minimax lower bounds for genuinely two-stage problems and identifies other Bayesian optimization utilities as untested future work. Existing smoothness and MLKQ limitations remain.

D1.justification: Section 5 newly specifies two uniformly sampled initial Bayesian optimization points and Delta=0.01. New Appendix F.5 supplies the three objective formulas and domains and explains reuse of precomputed weights across iterations. These document existing experiments; the code-access link is unchanged.

R1.justification: V2 adds Mala (2024) for healthcare value of information and Chen and Reiss (2011), Meunier et al. (2024), and Zhang et al. (2025) for the two-stage minimax discussion. The broader positioning against Monte Carlo methods and conditional Bayesian quadrature is retained.

P1.justification: Most prose and section order remain. Local edits shorten Remark 4.2, label the existing MLMC/QMC discussion as Remark 4.3, rename the healthcare paragraph, and add an Impact Statement and Appendix F.5.

P2.justification: The single-column manuscript becomes an ICML-format document with two-column main text and references and reformatted appendices. Figures 2–3 change from side-by-side to stacked panels; other figures and tables are resized or relocated. This substantially changes presentation while retaining the empirical plots.

improvement.justification: Aligning Theorem 1's density assumption with Appendix A and correcting cost exponents improves the precision of the central analysis. Added Bayesian optimization details aid reproducibility. These limited gains are partly offset by the inconsistent norm subscripts introduced in equation (F.42); the empirical evidence and main conclusions remain unchanged.
